title: Climate shock becomes economic adaptation
subtitle: Gulf of Maine, 1815–1820
description: A volcanic-climate shock altered temperatures, fish phenology and food pressure; fishers shifted effort and the emergency response became a lasting economic transition.

title: Weather shock becomes a subsistence crisis
subtitle: Czech Lands, 1816–1817
description: Cold and persistent wet weather damaged grain production; the harvest shock propagated into food scarcity and grain-price pressure with a measurable lag into 1817.

title: Cold years store risk in the water system
subtitle: Alpine Rhine Basin, 1816–1817
description: Post-eruption cold and snow conditions increased snow storage. In 1817, spring snowfall, snowmelt and intense rain combined in major Rhine and Lake Constance flooding.

title: Climate becomes cultural context
subtitle: Geneva, summer 1816
description: The unusually cold and cloudy Geneva summer created the documented setting in which Mary Godwin's literary circle stayed indoors, exchanged ghost stories and generated the story that became Frankenstein.

title: The same volcanic forcing, a different regional expression
subtitle: Qing China, 1815–1817 context
description: Proxy evidence shows severe cold, frost, snow and ice in southern China while hydroclimate evidence is spatially mixed, illustrating why WorldThreads must preserve regional variation and proxy disagreement.

title: Direct volcanic destruction and local subsistence
subtitle: Sumbawa · 1815 antecedent to the 1816 climate threads
description: Follow local ash damage, famine and documented relief. Annual aftermath timing and relief effectiveness remain uncertain. This illustrates the production and subsistence portion of the mechanism; no price series is supplied.

title: Volcanic forcing and monsoon reconstruction
subtitle: Asia · 1815–1817 context
description: Connect volcanic forcing to a regional drying reconstruction without inferring local crop loss or disease.

title: Colonial orders, violence and restrictions
subtitle: Oceania · 1815–1817 context
description: Trace punitive expeditions and policy in Australia through records with conflicting official accounts. No Tambora connection is asserted.

title: Military preparation across a mountain barrier
subtitle: South America · 1815–1817 context
description: Follow 1816 organization into the 1817 crossing and battle. Preparation is contributory; battle sequence is chronological.

title: Grain reserves and imports face delays and access limits
subtitle: Netherlands, 1816–1817
description: Compare stock monitoring, imports and subsidized sales. Policy intentions do not establish relief effectiveness.

title: Crop sensitivity does not fully explain human vulnerability
subtitle: Switzerland, 1816–1818
description: Model estimates and observed nutrition patterns are distinct. Crop differences and social mediation qualify a simple production-to-hunger chain.

title: Cold and rain have different causal attribution
subtitle: Europe, summer 1816
description: Modern simulations distinguish volcanic cooling from rainfall’s stronger dependence on circulation. Attribution probabilities are model-specific.

title: Local climate measurements and crop expectations
subtitle: Virginia, spring–summer 1816
description: Follow contemporaneous weather observations into reported fruit damage and a maize forecast. Forecasts are preserved as forecasts.

title: Korean harvest counterexample: climate anomaly with rice recovery
subtitle: Asia · 1816 and dated context
description: Records distinguish reported conditions, administrative classifications and interpretations; no volcanic disease attribution is asserted.

title: Bengal epidemic evidence without forced volcanic attribution
subtitle: Asia · 1816 and dated context
description: Records distinguish reported conditions, administrative classifications and interpretations; no volcanic disease attribution is asserted.

title: Bali direct ash damage and prolonged subsistence-health crisis
subtitle: Asia · 1816 and dated context
description: Records distinguish reported conditions, administrative classifications and interpretations; no volcanic disease attribution is asserted.

title: Irish scarcity and fever response
subtitle: Europe · 1816 and dated context
description: Records distinguish reported conditions, administrative classifications and interpretations; no volcanic disease attribution is asserted.

title: Foreign artists → royal patronage → proposed applied instruction
subtitle: South America · 1816 and dated context
description: Arrival, funding authorization and stated industrial aims are distinct from an institution actually opening.

title: Heavy rain → river inundation → threatened grain supply
subtitle: Oceania · 1816 and dated context
description: Local weather and inundation threaten food supply. Price effects and final harvest losses remain open.

title: Pacific routes carry food and diplomatic objects
subtitle: Oceania · 1816 and dated context
description: A comparison of two maritime exchanges, not a common causal chain. Colonial reports do not supply destination perspectives.

title: Asante diplomacy, restored sea routes and prestige goods
subtitle: Africa · 1816 and dated context
description: Independent of Tambora; envoy’s war explanation is attributed, not independently established.

title: Mauritius–Madagascar diplomacy and limits of anti-slave-trade law
subtitle: Africa · 1816 and dated context
description: Preserve Malagasy agency; laws are not enforcement results. No climate attribution.

title: Marine cooling, local contrasts and ocean memory
subtitle: Oceans · 1816 and dated context
description: Do not convert proxy, air thermometer and simulated heat content into interchangeable measurements; do not use basin-scale cooling to infer local crop or fishing failure.
